comparisons.peer_topic: VaR exception frequency and business model impact
comparisons.peer_summary: Net losses exceeding the 95% one-day VaR (exceptions) occurred on two occasions in 2024 and one occasion in 2023; the frequency of exceptions correlates with net revenue performance, with fewer exceptions expected during periods of significant positive net revenue days.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs disclose VaR backtesting exception frequencies for 2024. JPMorgan reported eight exceptions over the year, while Goldman Sachs reported two. Goldman Sachs additionally explains that exception frequency correlates with business model performance, noting that positive net revenue days generally lead to fewer exceptions, whereas adverse impacts on franchise revenues result in more loss days and more exceptions. JPMorgan does not provide this specific causal explanation in the cited text, but both firms report on the occurrence of backtesting exceptions as a measure of model risk.

sentences.text: For the 12 months ended December 31, 2024, the Firm posted backtesting gains on 179 of the 260 days, and observed eight VaR backtesting exceptions, of which three were in the three months ended December 31, 2024.
Net losses incurred on a single day for such positions exceeded our 95% one-day VaR (i.e., a VaR exception) on two occasions during 2024 and on one occasion during 2023.

During periods in which we have significantly more positive net revenue days than net revenue loss days, we expect to have fewer VaR exceptions because, under normal conditions, our business model generally produces positive net revenues.

comparisons.peer_topic: VaR Model Evaluation and 2024 Exceedance Statistics
comparisons.peer_summary: The firm evaluates its VaR model by comparing potential declines with actual trading results and examining drivers for losses exceeding the statistic. In 2024, there were 11 trading loss days, none exceeding 95% Total Management VaR, compared to 16 days in 2023 with one exceeding the limit.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley report VaR backtesting results and exception counts for 2024. Morgan Stanley reported 11 trading loss days with zero exceptions exceeding the 95% Total Management VaR, whereas JPMorgan reported eight VaR backtesting exceptions. Morgan Stanley also outlines its methodology for evaluating the VaR model by comparing potential declines with actual trading results and examining drivers for losses exceeding the statistic, similar to the context implied by JPMorgan's reporting on backtesting gains and losses.
